6. Output: output value, including the meaning, the format, and the value ranges if necessary;
7. Pre-condition: the condition that the system and the input must satisfy before the operation is executed;
8. Post-condition: the condition that the system and the output must satisfy after the operation is executed.

Finish this task by following the guidelines below.
1. Take the principle of modularization into account.
2. For each operation, determine its functional boundary based on the given requirement. Ensure high cohesion and low coupling.

# Requirement
```text
## 1. Overall 

This system turns plain structured text into a document outline tree. It is intended for texts whose section headings are marked by ordered level indicators, such as Arabic numbers, Roman numerals, Chinese numerals, letters, or circled numbers. The main semantic task is to recognize heading lines, convert their numbering into comparable level sequences, preserve ordinary text as section content, and reconstruct the parent-child hierarchy of the document.

## 2. Functional Requirement

Heading recognition is pattern-driven. Patterns are tried in order, and the first valid pattern determines both the heading level sequence and its priority. A line that does not match a valid heading should be treated as content belonging to the current section. Even an empty or unmatched document should still produce a synthetic root section titled `"ROOT"`.

Number conversion should treat each supported numbering family according to its natural ordering. Roman numerals should be case-insensitive and support standard subtractive forms. Chinese numerals should support common simplified and traditional digit variants, units, large magnitudes, and signed values. Letters map alphabetically, and circled numbers map to their represented numeric value. Invalid numeric text should not create a valid heading level.

Tree construction is based on the integer level sequence of each parsed heading. A root node has an empty sequence. A child sequence extends its parent sequence, while siblings share the same prefix and advance by level order. Strict construction should reject chains that do not begin with the root. The more tolerant construction strategy should recover from irregular jumps by moving back to the nearest suitable ancestor before attaching the next node.For the auto-prune strategy, the builder should maintain the latest valid branch from the root to the current node. If the next chain node is an immediate valid next node according to the level-sequence relation, it should be attached to the nearest ancestor whose level sequence is the prefix of the new node, and the current branch should be updated.

If a chain node is not an immediate valid next node, it should be stored in a pending queue rather than attached immediately. When a later immediate node is found, pending nodes before it should be merged into the current node's content in arrival order. If the pending queue reaches three nodes, the strategy should check whether all pending nodes form an immediate sibling sequence. If so, they should be attached to the tree in order; otherwise, the oldest pending node should be merged into the current node's content. After all input nodes are processed, any remaining pending nodes should be merged into the current node's content.

When section content is merged or collected from descendants, content should be concatenated in traversal order without inserting extra separators. Parent-child links should remain consistent when tree nodes are attached.

Export behavior must be deterministic. Chain export should use one line per node in the form `LEVEL-<levelSeq>: <title>`. Tree JSON export should preserve child order and use the field names `title`, `level_seq`, `level_text`, `content`, and `children`, with stable pretty-printing using four-space indentation.

## 3. External / Tool Classes

`Utils` is an external numeric utility used by the parser for Roman numeral and Chinese numeral conversion.
```

class AutoPruneStrategy {
    addNodeAndUpdateBranch(node : ChainNode, currentBranch : List<TreeNode>) : void
    addNodeToTree(node : ChainNode, currentBranch : List<TreeNode>, currentNodeRef : node) : void
    buildTree(chain : List<ChainNode>) : TreeNode
    createTreeNode(chainnode : ChainNode) : TreeNode
    isAllNotImmNodesSiblings(queue : Deque) : void
}
class BaseNode {
    content : String
    levelSeq : List<int>
    levelText : String
    title : String
    concatNode(node : BaseNode) : void
}
class ChainNode {
    patternPriority : int
}
class ChainParser {
    patterns : List<LevelPattern>
    createChainNode(levelSeq : List<int>, title : String, content : String, levelText : String, patternPriority : int) : ChainNode
    detectLevel(line : String) : ChainNode
    parseToChain(text : String) : List<ChainNode>
}

    description : String
    failOnConvert : boolean
    fixedLevelSeq : List<EIntegerObject>
    maxLevel : int
    minLevel : int
    numberType : NumberType
    regexText : String
    separator : String
    helper : ParserHelper
    convertMatchedText(matchedText : String) : List<EIntegerObject>
    getRegex() : Pattern
}

    convertNumber(numberType : NumberType, text : String) : EIntegerObject
    getNumberPattern(numberType : NumberType) : String
}

    maxLevel : int
    minLevel : int
    numberType : NumberType
    prefixRegex : String
    separator : String
    suffixRegex : String
    build() : LevelPattern
    copySelf() : PatternBuilder
    modify(newPrefixRegex : String, newMinLevel : int) : PatternBuilder
    validate() : void
}
class StrictStrategy {
    buildTree(chain : List<ChainNode>) : TreeNode
    createTreeNode(chainnode : ChainNode) : TreeNode
    isChild(parentSeq : List<EIntegerObject>, childSeq : List<EIntegerObject>) : boolean
}

    strategy : TreeBuildingStrategy
    buildTree(chain : List<ChainNode>) : TreeNode
}
abstract class TreeBuildingStrategy {
    buildTree(chain : List<ChainNode>) : TreeNode
    getLastLevel(levelSeq : List<EIntegerObject>) : int
    getPrefix(levelSeq : List<EIntegerObject>) : List<EIntegerObject>
    isImmNext(frontSeq : List<EIntegerObject>, backSeq : List<EIntegerObject>) : boolean
    isRoot(node : BaseNode) : boolean
}
class TreeExporter {
    escapeJson(s : String) : String
    exportChain(chain : List<ChainNode>) : String
    exportToJson(tree : TreeNode) : String
    exportToJsonFile(tree : TreeNode, filePath : Path) : void
    exportTree(tree : TreeNode) : String
    exportTreeInternal(node : TreeNode, prefix : String, isLast : boolean, isRoot : boolean) : String
    nodeToDict(node : TreeNode) : EMap
    toJson(obj : EJavaObject, indent : int) : String
}
class TreeNode {
    children : List<TreeNode>
    parent : TreeNode
    addChild(child : TreeNode) : void
    getFullContent() : String
    mergeAllChildren() : void
}
enum NumberType {
    ARABIC
    ROMAN
    CHINESE
    LETTER
    CIRCLED
}

    concatNode(node : BaseNode) : void
}
class ChainNode {
    patternPriority : int
}
class ChainParser {
    patterns : List<LevelPattern>
    createChainNode(levelSeq : List<int>, title : String, content : String, levelText : String, patternPriority : int) : ChainNode
    detectLevel(line : String) : ChainNode
    parseToChain(text : String) : List<ChainNode>
}
class LevelPattern {
    description : String
    failOnConvert : boolean
    fixedLevelSeq : List<EIntegerObject>
    maxLevel : int
    minLevel : int
    numberType : NumberType
    regexText : String
    separator : String
    helper : ParserHelper
    convertMatchedText(matchedText : String) : List<EIntegerObject>
    getRegex() : Pattern
}
class ParserHelper {
    convertNumber(numberType : NumberType, text : String) : EIntegerObject
    getNumberPattern(numberType : NumberType) : String
}
class PatternBuilder {
    maxLevel : int
    minLevel : int
    numberType : NumberType
    prefixRegex : String
    separator : String
    suffixRegex : String
    build() : LevelPattern
    copySelf() : PatternBuilder
    modify(newPrefixRegex : String, newMinLevel : int) : PatternBuilder
    validate() : void
}
class StrictStrategy {
    buildTree(chain : List<ChainNode>) : TreeNode
    createTreeNode(chainnode : ChainNode) : TreeNode
    isChild(parentSeq : List<EIntegerObject>, childSeq : List<EIntegerObject>) : boolean
}
class TreeBuilder {
    strategy : TreeBuildingStrategy
    buildTree(chain : List<ChainNode>) : TreeNode
}
abstract class TreeBuildingStrategy {
    buildTree(chain : List<ChainNode>) : TreeNode
    getLastLevel(levelSeq : List<EIntegerObject>) : int
    getPrefix(levelSeq : List<EIntegerObject>) : List<EIntegerObject>
    isImmNext(frontSeq : List<EIntegerObject>, backSeq : List<EIntegerObject>) : boolean
    isRoot(node : BaseNode) : boolean
}
class TreeExporter {
    escapeJson(s : String) : String
    exportChain(chain : List<ChainNode>) : String
    exportToJson(tree : TreeNode) : String
    exportToJsonFile(tree : TreeNode, filePath : Path) : void
    exportTree(tree : TreeNode) : String
    exportTreeInternal(node : TreeNode, prefix : String, isLast : boolean, isRoot : boolean) : String
    nodeToDict(node : TreeNode) : EMap
    toJson(obj : EJavaObject, indent : int) : String
}
class TreeNode {
    children : List<TreeNode>
    parent : TreeNode
    addChild(child : TreeNode) : void
    getFullContent() : String
    mergeAllChildren() : void
}
enum NumberType {
    ARABIC
    ROMAN
    CHINESE
    LETTER
    CIRCLED
}

AutoPruneStrategy --|> TreeBuildingStrategy
ChainNode --|> BaseNode
ChainParser *-- "*" LevelPattern : patterns
LevelPattern --> ParserHelper : helper
StrictStrategy --|> TreeBuildingStrategy
TreeBuilder --> TreeBuildingStrategy : strategy
TreeNode --|> BaseNode
TreeNode *-- "*" TreeNode : children  'opposite: parent
TreeNode --> TreeNode : parent  'opposite: children
@enduml
```

# Requirement
```text
## 1. Overall 

This system turns plain structured text into a document outline tree. It is intended for texts whose section headings are marked by ordered level indicators, such as Arabic numbers, Roman numerals, Chinese numerals, letters, or circled numbers. The main semantic task is to recognize heading lines, convert their numbering into comparable level sequences, preserve ordinary text as section content, and reconstruct the parent-child hierarchy of the document.

## 2. Functional Requirement

Heading recognition is pattern-driven. Patterns are tried in order, and the first valid pattern determines both the heading level sequence and its priority. A line that does not match a valid heading should be treated as content belonging to the current section. Even an empty or unmatched document should still produce a synthetic root section titled `"ROOT"`.

Number conversion should treat each supported numbering family according to its natural ordering. Roman numerals should be case-insensitive and support standard subtractive forms. Chinese numerals should support common simplified and traditional digit variants, units, large magnitudes, and signed values. Letters map alphabetically, and circled numbers map to their represented numeric value. Invalid numeric text should not create a valid heading level.

Tree construction is based on the integer level sequence of each parsed heading. A root node has an empty sequence. A child sequence extends its parent sequence, while siblings share the same prefix and advance by level order. Strict construction should reject chains that do not begin with the root. The more tolerant construction strategy should recover from irregular jumps by moving back to the nearest suitable ancestor before attaching the next node.For the auto-prune strategy, the builder should maintain the latest valid branch from the root to the current node. If the next chain node is an immediate valid next node according to the level-sequence relation, it should be attached to the nearest ancestor whose level sequence is the prefix of the new node, and the current branch should be updated.

If a chain node is not an immediate valid next node, it should be stored in a pending queue rather than attached immediately. When a later immediate node is found, pending nodes before it should be merged into the current node's content in arrival order. If the pending queue reaches three nodes, the strategy should check whether all pending nodes form an immediate sibling sequence. If so, they should be attached to the tree in order; otherwise, the oldest pending node should be merged into the current node's content. After all input nodes are processed, any remaining pending nodes should be merged into the current node's content.

When section content is merged or collected from descendants, content should be concatenated in traversal order without inserting extra separators. Parent-child links should remain consistent when tree nodes are attached.

Export behavior must be deterministic. Chain export should use one line per node in the form `LEVEL-<levelSeq>: <title>`. Tree JSON export should preserve child order and use the field names `title`, `level_seq`, `level_text`, `content`, and `children`, with stable pretty-printing using four-space indentation.

## 3. External / Tool Classes

`Utils` is an external numeric utility used by the parser for Roman numeral and Chinese numeral conversion.
```

# Operation Specifications
PatternBuilder::validate
Summary: Validates the consistency of the builder before it is used to construct a LevelPattern.
Algorithm:
1. Check that numberType is non-null.
2. Check that minLevel >= 0 and maxLevel >= minLevel.

# Requirement
```text
## 1. Overall 

This system turns plain structured text into a document outline tree. It is intended for texts whose section headings are marked by ordered level indicators, such as Arabic numbers, Roman numerals, Chinese numerals, letters, or circled numbers. The main semantic task is to recognize heading lines, convert their numbering into comparable level sequences, preserve ordinary text as section content, and reconstruct the parent-child hierarchy of the document.

## 2. Functional Requirement

Heading recognition is pattern-driven. Patterns are tried in order, and the first valid pattern determines both the heading level sequence and its priority. A line that does not match a valid heading should be treated as content belonging to the current section. Even an empty or unmatched document should still produce a synthetic root section titled `"ROOT"`.

Number conversion should treat each supported numbering family according to its natural ordering. Roman numerals should be case-insensitive and support standard subtractive forms. Chinese numerals should support common simplified and traditional digit variants, units, large magnitudes, and signed values. Letters map alphabetically, and circled numbers map to their represented numeric value. Invalid numeric text should not create a valid heading level.

Tree construction is based on the integer level sequence of each parsed heading. A root node has an empty sequence. A child sequence extends its parent sequence, while siblings share the same prefix and advance by level order. Strict construction should reject chains that do not begin with the root. The more tolerant construction strategy should recover from irregular jumps by moving back to the nearest suitable ancestor before attaching the next node.For the auto-prune strategy, the builder should maintain the latest valid branch from the root to the current node. If the next chain node is an immediate valid next node according to the level-sequence relation, it should be attached to the nearest ancestor whose level sequence is the prefix of the new node, and the current branch should be updated.

If a chain node is not an immediate valid next node, it should be stored in a pending queue rather than attached immediately. When a later immediate node is found, pending nodes before it should be merged into the current node's content in arrival order. If the pending queue reaches three nodes, the strategy should check whether all pending nodes form an immediate sibling sequence. If so, they should be attached to the tree in order; otherwise, the oldest pending node should be merged into the current node's content. After all input nodes are processed, any remaining pending nodes should be merged into the current node's content.

When section content is merged or collected from descendants, content should be concatenated in traversal order without inserting extra separators. Parent-child links should remain consistent when tree nodes are attached.

Export behavior must be deterministic. Chain export should use one line per node in the form `LEVEL-<levelSeq>: <title>`. Tree JSON export should preserve child order and use the field names `title`, `level_seq`, `level_text`, `content`, and `children`, with stable pretty-printing using four-space indentation.

## 3. External / Tool Classes

`Utils` is an external numeric utility used by the parser for Roman numeral and Chinese numeral conversion.
```

# Requirement
```text
## 1. Overall 

This system turns plain structured text into a document outline tree. It is intended for texts whose section headings are marked by ordered level indicators, such as Arabic numbers, Roman numerals, Chinese numerals, letters, or circled numbers. The main semantic task is to recognize heading lines, convert their numbering into comparable level sequences, preserve ordinary text as section content, and reconstruct the parent-child hierarchy of the document.

## 2. Functional Requirement

Heading recognition is pattern-driven. Patterns are tried in order, and the first valid pattern determines both the heading level sequence and its priority. A line that does not match a valid heading should be treated as content belonging to the current section. Even an empty or unmatched document should still produce a synthetic root section titled `"ROOT"`.

Number conversion should treat each supported numbering family according to its natural ordering. Roman numerals should be case-insensitive and support standard subtractive forms. Chinese numerals should support common simplified and traditional digit variants, units, large magnitudes, and signed values. Letters map alphabetically, and circled numbers map to their represented numeric value. Invalid numeric text should not create a valid heading level.

Tree construction is based on the integer level sequence of each parsed heading. A root node has an empty sequence. A child sequence extends its parent sequence, while siblings share the same prefix and advance by level order. Strict construction should reject chains that do not begin with the root. The more tolerant construction strategy should recover from irregular jumps by moving back to the nearest suitable ancestor before attaching the next node.For the auto-prune strategy, the builder should maintain the latest valid branch from the root to the current node. If the next chain node is an immediate valid next node according to the level-sequence relation, it should be attached to the nearest ancestor whose level sequence is the prefix of the new node, and the current branch should be updated.

If a chain node is not an immediate valid next node, it should be stored in a pending queue rather than attached immediately. When a later immediate node is found, pending nodes before it should be merged into the current node's content in arrival order. If the pending queue reaches three nodes, the strategy should check whether all pending nodes form an immediate sibling sequence. If so, they should be attached to the tree in order; otherwise, the oldest pending node should be merged into the current node's content. After all input nodes are processed, any remaining pending nodes should be merged into the current node's content.

When section content is merged or collected from descendants, content should be concatenated in traversal order without inserting extra separators. Parent-child links should remain consistent when tree nodes are attached.

Export behavior must be deterministic. Chain export should use one line per node in the form `LEVEL-<levelSeq>: <title>`. Tree JSON export should preserve child order and use the field names `title`, `level_seq`, `level_text`, `content`, and `children`, with stable pretty-printing using four-space indentation.

## 3. External / Tool Classes

`Utils` is an external numeric utility used by the parser for Roman numeral and Chinese numeral conversion.

# Operation Specifications
TreeNode::getFullContent
Summary: Returns the concatenated content of this node and all descendants in pre-order traversal, without inserting separators.
Algorithm:
1. Create a StringBuilder.
2. Append this.content if non-null.
3. For each child in children, append child.getFullContent().
4. Return the resulting string.
Related Features: BaseNode.content, TreeNode.children
Related Classes: TreeNode, BaseNode
Input: none.
Output: String — full accumulated content.
Pre-condition: none.
Post-condition: The output is deterministic; no separators are added.

TreeNode::mergeAllChildren
Summary: Merges the full content of all children into this node's content and removes the children from the tree.
Algorithm:
1. For each child in children:
   a. Append child.getFullContent() to this.content.
   b. Set child.parent = null.
2. Clear the children list.
Related Features: BaseNode.content, TreeNode.children, TreeNode.parent, TreeNode.getFullContent
Related Classes: TreeNode, BaseNode
Input: none.
Output: void.
Pre-condition: none.
Post-condition: This node contains its own content plus all descendant content in traversal order; children list is empty.

TreeNode::addChild
Summary: Adds a child TreeNode to this node at the end of the children list and maintains the parent pointer.
Algorithm:
1. If child is null or child == this, return.
2. If child.parent is not null, remove child from its old parent's children list.
3. Add child to this.children.
4. Set child.parent = this.
Related Features: TreeNode.children, TreeNode.parent
Related Classes: TreeNode
Input: child — TreeNode or null.
Output: void.
Pre-condition: none.
Post-condition: child is at the end of this.children; child.parent == this; no duplicate child remains.

# Task
You will be given a **Requirement** and a **Class Diagram** in PlantUML. Your task is to annotate every operation listed in **Operations** with a specification.

An operation specification must describe the following sections about the operation:
1. Summary: the summary of functionality;
2. Algorithm: algorithm or pseudo code;
3. Related Features: a list of structural or behavior features within this class that shall be accessed;
4. Related Classes: a list of classes and data types defined in **Class Diagram** that shall be accessed, in the format of `Related Classes: ClsA, CLsB, ...` or `Related Classes: None`;
5. Input: the input parameters, including the meaning, the format, and the value ranges if necessary;
6. Output: output value, including the meaning, the format, and the value ranges if necessary;
7. Pre-condition: the condition that the system and the input must satisfy before the operation is executed;
8. Post-condition: the condition that the system and the output must satisfy after the operation is executed.

Finish this task by following the guidelines below.
1. Take the principle of modularization into account.
2. For each operation, determine its functional boundary based on the given requirement. Ensure high cohesion and low coupling.
3. If there is any unspecified details, such as undefined constants, rates, and ratios, then you must infer them.
4. Make sure that all requirements can be covered.

# Requirement
```text
## 1. Overall 

This system turns plain structured text into a document outline tree. It is intended for texts whose section headings are marked by ordered level indicators, such as Arabic numbers, Roman numerals, Chinese numerals, letters, or circled numbers. The main semantic task is to recognize heading lines, convert their numbering into comparable level sequences, preserve ordinary text as section content, and reconstruct the parent-child hierarchy of the document.

## 2. Functional Requirement

Heading recognition is pattern-driven. Patterns are tried in order, and the first valid pattern determines both the heading level sequence and its priority. A line that does not match a valid heading should be treated as content belonging to the current section. Even an empty or unmatched document should still produce a synthetic root section titled `"ROOT"`.

Number conversion should treat each supported numbering family according to its natural ordering. Roman numerals should be case-insensitive and support standard subtractive forms. Chinese numerals should support common simplified and traditional digit variants, units, large magnitudes, and signed values. Letters map alphabetically, and circled numbers map to their represented numeric value. Invalid numeric text should not create a valid heading level.

Tree construction is based on the integer level sequence of each parsed heading. A root node has an empty sequence. A child sequence extends its parent sequence, while siblings share the same prefix and advance by level order. Strict construction should reject chains that do not begin with the root. The more tolerant construction strategy should recover from irregular jumps by moving back to the nearest suitable ancestor before attaching the next node.For the auto-prune strategy, the builder should maintain the latest valid branch from the root to the current node. If the next chain node is an immediate valid next node according to the level-sequence relation, it should be attached to the nearest ancestor whose level sequence is the prefix of the new node, and the current branch should be updated.

If a chain node is not an immediate valid next node, it should be stored in a pending queue rather than attached immediately. When a later immediate node is found, pending nodes before it should be merged into the current node's content in arrival order. If the pending queue reaches three nodes, the strategy should check whether all pending nodes form an immediate sibling sequence. If so, they should be attached to the tree in order; otherwise, the oldest pending node should be merged into the current node's content. After all input nodes are processed, any remaining pending nodes should be merged into the current node's content.

When section content is merged or collected from descendants, content should be concatenated in traversal order without inserting extra separators. Parent-child links should remain consistent when tree nodes are attached.

Export behavior must be deterministic. Chain export should use one line per node in the form `LEVEL-<levelSeq>: <title>`. Tree JSON export should preserve child order and use the field names `title`, `level_seq`, `level_text`, `content`, and `children`, with stable pretty-printing using four-space indentation.

## 3. External / Tool Classes

`Utils` is an external numeric utility used by the parser for Roman numeral and Chinese numeral conversion.
```

# Requirement
```text
## 1. Overall 

This system turns plain structured text into a document outline tree. It is intended for texts whose section headings are marked by ordered level indicators, such as Arabic numbers, Roman numerals, Chinese numerals, letters, or circled numbers. The main semantic task is to recognize heading lines, convert their numbering into comparable level sequences, preserve ordinary text as section content, and reconstruct the parent-child hierarchy of the document.

## 2. Functional Requirement

Heading recognition is pattern-driven. Patterns are tried in order, and the first valid pattern determines both the heading level sequence and its priority. A line that does not match a valid heading should be treated as content belonging to the current section. Even an empty or unmatched document should still produce a synthetic root section titled `"ROOT"`.

Number conversion should treat each supported numbering family according to its natural ordering. Roman numerals should be case-insensitive and support standard subtractive forms. Chinese numerals should support common simplified and traditional digit variants, units, large magnitudes, and signed values. Letters map alphabetically, and circled numbers map to their represented numeric value. Invalid numeric text should not create a valid heading level.

Tree construction is based on the integer level sequence of each parsed heading. A root node has an empty sequence. A child sequence extends its parent sequence, while siblings share the same prefix and advance by level order. Strict construction should reject chains that do not begin with the root. The more tolerant construction strategy should recover from irregular jumps by moving back to the nearest suitable ancestor before attaching the next node.For the auto-prune strategy, the builder should maintain the latest valid branch from the root to the current node. If the next chain node is an immediate valid next node according to the level-sequence relation, it should be attached to the nearest ancestor whose level sequence is the prefix of the new node, and the current branch should be updated.

If a chain node is not an immediate valid next node, it should be stored in a pending queue rather than attached immediately. When a later immediate node is found, pending nodes before it should be merged into the current node's content in arrival order. If the pending queue reaches three nodes, the strategy should check whether all pending nodes form an immediate sibling sequence. If so, they should be attached to the tree in order; otherwise, the oldest pending node should be merged into the current node's content. After all input nodes are processed, any remaining pending nodes should be merged into the current node's content.

When section content is merged or collected from descendants, content should be concatenated in traversal order without inserting extra separators. Parent-child links should remain consistent when tree nodes are attached.

Export behavior must be deterministic. Chain export should use one line per node in the form `LEVEL-<levelSeq>: <title>`. Tree JSON export should preserve child order and use the field names `title`, `level_seq`, `level_text`, `content`, and `children`, with stable pretty-printing using four-space indentation.

## 3. External / Tool Classes

`Utils` is an external numeric utility used by the parser for Roman numeral and Chinese numeral conversion.
```

# Requirement
```text
## 1. Overall 

This system turns plain structured text into a document outline tree. It is intended for texts whose section headings are marked by ordered level indicators, such as Arabic numbers, Roman numerals, Chinese numerals, letters, or circled numbers. The main semantic task is to recognize heading lines, convert their numbering into comparable level sequences, preserve ordinary text as section content, and reconstruct the parent-child hierarchy of the document.

## 2. Functional Requirement

Heading recognition is pattern-driven. Patterns are tried in order, and the first valid pattern determines both the heading level sequence and its priority. A line that does not match a valid heading should be treated as content belonging to the current section. Even an empty or unmatched document should still produce a synthetic root section titled `"ROOT"`.

Number conversion should treat each supported numbering family according to its natural ordering. Roman numerals should be case-insensitive and support standard subtractive forms. Chinese numerals should support common simplified and traditional digit variants, units, large magnitudes, and signed values. Letters map alphabetically, and circled numbers map to their represented numeric value. Invalid numeric text should not create a valid heading level.

Tree construction is based on the integer level sequence of each parsed heading. A root node has an empty sequence. A child sequence extends its parent sequence, while siblings share the same prefix and advance by level order. Strict construction should reject chains that do not begin with the root. The more tolerant construction strategy should recover from irregular jumps by moving back to the nearest suitable ancestor before attaching the next node.For the auto-prune strategy, the builder should maintain the latest valid branch from the root to the current node. If the next chain node is an immediate valid next node according to the level-sequence relation, it should be attached to the nearest ancestor whose level sequence is the prefix of the new node, and the current branch should be updated.

If a chain node is not an immediate valid next node, it should be stored in a pending queue rather than attached immediately. When a later immediate node is found, pending nodes before it should be merged into the current node's content in arrival order. If the pending queue reaches three nodes, the strategy should check whether all pending nodes form an immediate sibling sequence. If so, they should be attached to the tree in order; otherwise, the oldest pending node should be merged into the current node's content. After all input nodes are processed, any remaining pending nodes should be merged into the current node's content.

When section content is merged or collected from descendants, content should be concatenated in traversal order without inserting extra separators. Parent-child links should remain consistent when tree nodes are attached.

Export behavior must be deterministic. Chain export should use one line per node in the form `LEVEL-<levelSeq>: <title>`. Tree JSON export should preserve child order and use the field names `title`, `level_seq`, `level_text`, `content`, and `children`, with stable pretty-printing using four-space indentation.

## 3. External / Tool Classes

`Utils` is an external numeric utility used by the parser for Roman numeral and Chinese numeral conversion.
```

PatternBuilder::validate
Summary: Validates that this PatternBuilder configuration is usable for building a LevelPattern.
Algorithm:
  1. Check minLevel >= 1; otherwise throw IllegalArgumentException.
  2. Check maxLevel >= minLevel; otherwise throw IllegalArgumentException.

  4. Check prefixRegex, suffixRegex, and separator are non-null.

Related Features: minLevel, maxLevel, numberType, prefixRegex, suffixRegex, separator
Related Classes: PatternBuilder, NumberType, Pattern
Input: none
Output: void

Summary: Creates an independent copy of this PatternBuilder.
Algorithm:
  1. Create a new PatternBuilder.
  2. Copy maxLevel, minLevel, numberType, prefixRegex, separator, and suffixRegex into it.
  3. Return the copy.
Related Features: maxLevel, minLevel, numberType, prefixRegex, separator, suffixRegex
Related Classes: PatternBuilder, NumberType
Input: none
Output: A new PatternBuilder with the same configuration.
Pre-condition: none.
Post-condition: The original builder is unchanged; modifications to the copy do not affect the original.

PatternBuilder::modify
Summary: Returns a new builder based on the current one, replacing the prefix regex and minimum level.
Algorithm:
  1. copy = copySelf().
  2. copy.prefixRegex = newPrefixRegex.
  3. copy.minLevel = newMinLevel.
  4. Return copy.
Related Features: copySelf, prefixRegex, minLevel
Related Classes: PatternBuilder
Input: newPrefixRegex: String; newMinLevel: int.
Output: A modified copy of this PatternBuilder.
Pre-condition: newPrefixRegex is non-null; newMinLevel is a positive integer.
Post-condition: The returned builder has the new prefix regex and minimum level; the current builder is unchanged.

# Requirement
```text
## 1. Overall 

This system turns plain structured text into a document outline tree. It is intended for texts whose section headings are marked by ordered level indicators, such as Arabic numbers, Roman numerals, Chinese numerals, letters, or circled numbers. The main semantic task is to recognize heading lines, convert their numbering into comparable level sequences, preserve ordinary text as section content, and reconstruct the parent-child hierarchy of the document.

## 2. Functional Requirement

Heading recognition is pattern-driven. Patterns are tried in order, and the first valid pattern determines both the heading level sequence and its priority. A line that does not match a valid heading should be treated as content belonging to the current section. Even an empty or unmatched document should still produce a synthetic root section titled `"ROOT"`.

Number conversion should treat each supported numbering family according to its natural ordering. Roman numerals should be case-insensitive and support standard subtractive forms. Chinese numerals should support common simplified and traditional digit variants, units, large magnitudes, and signed values. Letters map alphabetically, and circled numbers map to their represented numeric value. Invalid numeric text should not create a valid heading level.

Tree construction is based on the integer level sequence of each parsed heading. A root node has an empty sequence. A child sequence extends its parent sequence, while siblings share the same prefix and advance by level order. Strict construction should reject chains that do not begin with the root. The more tolerant construction strategy should recover from irregular jumps by moving back to the nearest suitable ancestor before attaching the next node.For the auto-prune strategy, the builder should maintain the latest valid branch from the root to the current node. If the next chain node is an immediate valid next node according to the level-sequence relation, it should be attached to the nearest ancestor whose level sequence is the prefix of the new node, and the current branch should be updated.

If a chain node is not an immediate valid next node, it should be stored in a pending queue rather than attached immediately. When a later immediate node is found, pending nodes before it should be merged into the current node's content in arrival order. If the pending queue reaches three nodes, the strategy should check whether all pending nodes form an immediate sibling sequence. If so, they should be attached to the tree in order; otherwise, the oldest pending node should be merged into the current node's content. After all input nodes are processed, any remaining pending nodes should be merged into the current node's content.

When section content is merged or collected from descendants, content should be concatenated in traversal order without inserting extra separators. Parent-child links should remain consistent when tree nodes are attached.

Export behavior must be deterministic. Chain export should use one line per node in the form `LEVEL-<levelSeq>: <title>`. Tree JSON export should preserve child order and use the field names `title`, `level_seq`, `level_text`, `content`, and `children`, with stable pretty-printing using four-space indentation.

## 3. External / Tool Classes

`Utils` is an external numeric utility used by the parser for Roman numeral and Chinese numeral conversion.
```

If the next chain node is an immediate valid next node according to the level-sequence relation, it should be attached to the nearest ancestor whose level sequence is the prefix of the new node, and the current branch should be updated.

If a chain node is not an immediate valid next node, it should be stored in a pending queue rather than attached immediately. When a later immediate node is found, pending nodes before it should be merged into the current node's content in arrival order. If the pending queue reaches three nodes, the strategy should check whether all pending nodes form an immediate sibling sequence. If so, they should be attached to the tree in order; otherwise, the oldest pending node should be merged into the current node's content. After all input nodes are processed, any remaining pending nodes should be merged into the current node's content.

When section content is merged or collected from descendants, content should be concatenated in traversal order without inserting extra separators. Parent-child links should remain consistent when tree nodes are attached.

Export behavior must be deterministic. Chain export should use one line per node in the form `LEVEL-<levelSeq>: <title>`. Tree JSON export should preserve child order and use the field names `title`, `level_seq`, `level_text`, `content`, and `children`, with stable pretty-printing using four-space indentation.

# Requirement
```text
## 1. Overall 

This system turns plain structured text into a document outline tree. It is intended for texts whose section headings are marked by ordered level indicators, such as Arabic numbers, Roman numerals, Chinese numerals, letters, or circled numbers. The main semantic task is to recognize heading lines, convert their numbering into comparable level sequences, preserve ordinary text as section content, and reconstruct the parent-child hierarchy of the document.

## 2. Functional Requirement

Heading recognition is pattern-driven. Patterns are tried in order, and the first valid pattern determines both the heading level sequence and its priority. A line that does not match a valid heading should be treated as content belonging to the current section. Even an empty or unmatched document should still produce a synthetic root section titled `"ROOT"`.

Number conversion should treat each supported numbering family according to its natural ordering. Roman numerals should be case-insensitive and support standard subtractive forms. Chinese numerals should support common simplified and traditional digit variants, units, large magnitudes, and signed values. Letters map alphabetically, and circled numbers map to their represented numeric value. Invalid numeric text should not create a valid heading level.

Tree construction is based on the integer level sequence of each parsed heading. A root node has an empty sequence. A child sequence extends its parent sequence, while siblings share the same prefix and advance by level order. Strict construction should reject chains that do not begin with the root. The more tolerant construction strategy should recover from irregular jumps by moving back to the nearest suitable ancestor before attaching the next node.For the auto-prune strategy, the builder should maintain the latest valid branch from the root to the current node. If the next chain node is an immediate valid next node according to the level-sequence relation, it should be attached to the nearest ancestor whose level sequence is the prefix of the new node, and the current branch should be updated.

If a chain node is not an immediate valid next node, it should be stored in a pending queue rather than attached immediately. When a later immediate node is found, pending nodes before it should be merged into the current node's content in arrival order. If the pending queue reaches three nodes, the strategy should check whether all pending nodes form an immediate sibling sequence. If so, they should be attached to the tree in order; otherwise, the oldest pending node should be merged into the current node's content. After all input nodes are processed, any remaining pending nodes should be merged into the current node's content.

When section content is merged or collected from descendants, content should be concatenated in traversal order without inserting extra separators. Parent-child links should remain consistent when tree nodes are attached.

Export behavior must be deterministic. Chain export should use one line per node in the form `LEVEL-<levelSeq>: <title>`. # Operation Specifications
TreeNode::getFullContent
Summary: Returns the concatenation of this node's content and the full content of all descendants in traversal order, without extra separators.
Algorithm:
  1. sb = new StringBuilder(content == null ? "" : content).
  2. For each child in children order, append child.getFullContent().
  3. Return sb.toString().
Related Features: content, children
Related Classes: TreeNode, List
Input: none
Output: String containing merged content in traversal order.
Pre-condition: none.
Post-condition: no tree state is changed.

TreeNode::mergeAllChildren
Summary: Merges all descendant content into this node's content and removes all child links.
Algorithm:
  1. merged = getFullContent().
  2. For each child, set child.parent = null.
  3. Clear children.
  4. Set this.content = merged.
Related Features: content, children, parent, getFullContent
Related Classes: TreeNode, List
Input: none
Output: void
Pre-condition: none.
Post-condition: this node's content contains all descendant content; children is empty; old children have null parent.

TreeNode::addChild
Summary: Adds a child to this node and maintains the bidirectional parent-child link.
Algorithm:
  1. If child is null, throw IllegalArgumentException.
  2. If child.parent is not null and not this, remove child from its old parent's children list.
  3. Set child.parent = this.
  4. If child is not already in children, add child to children.
Related Features: children, parent
Related Classes: TreeNode, List
Input: child: TreeNode.
Output: void
Pre-condition: child is non-null.
Post-condition: child is in this.children and child.parent == this; no duplicate child entries exist.

# Requirement
```text
## 1. Overall 

This system turns plain structured text into a document outline tree. It is intended for texts whose section headings are marked by ordered level indicators, such as Arabic numbers, Roman numerals, Chinese numerals, letters, or circled numbers. The main semantic task is to recognize heading lines, convert their numbering into comparable level sequences, preserve ordinary text as section content, and reconstruct the parent-child hierarchy of the document.

## 2. Functional Requirement

Heading recognition is pattern-driven. Patterns are tried in order, and the first valid pattern determines both the heading level sequence and its priority. A line that does not match a valid heading should be treated as content belonging to the current section. Even an empty or unmatched document should still produce a synthetic root section titled `"ROOT"`.

Number conversion should treat each supported numbering family according to its natural ordering. Roman numerals should be case-insensitive and support standard subtractive forms. Chinese numerals should support common simplified and traditional digit variants, units, large magnitudes, and signed values. Letters map alphabetically, and circled numbers map to their represented numeric value. Invalid numeric text should not create a valid heading level.

Tree construction is based on the integer level sequence of each parsed heading. A root node has an empty sequence. A child sequence extends its parent sequence, while siblings share the same prefix and advance by level order. Strict construction should reject chains that do not begin with the root. The more tolerant construction strategy should recover from irregular jumps by moving back to the nearest suitable ancestor before attaching the next node.For the auto-prune strategy, the builder should maintain the latest valid branch from the root to the current node. If the next chain node is an immediate valid next node according to the level-sequence relation, it should be attached to the nearest ancestor whose level sequence is the prefix of the new node, and the current branch should be updated.

If a chain node is not an immediate valid next node, it should be stored in a pending queue rather than attached immediately. When a later immediate node is found, pending nodes before it should be merged into the current node's content in arrival order. If the pending queue reaches three nodes, the strategy should check whether all pending nodes form an immediate sibling sequence. If so, they should be attached to the tree in order; otherwise, the oldest pending node should be merged into the current node's content. After all input nodes are processed, any remaining pending nodes should be merged into the current node's content.

When section content is merged or collected from descendants, content should be concatenated in traversal order without inserting extra separators. Parent-child links should remain consistent when tree nodes are attached.

Export behavior must be deterministic. Chain export should use one line per node in the form `LEVEL-<levelSeq>: <title>`. Tree JSON export should preserve child order and use the field names `title`, `level_seq`, `level_text`, `content`, and `children`, with stable pretty-printing using four-space indentation.

## 3. External / Tool Classes

`Utils` is an external numeric utility used by the parser for Roman numeral and Chinese numeral conversion.

# Operation Specifications
AutoPruneStrategy::addNodeToTree
Summary: Low-level attachment of a ChainNode under a specified parent TreeNode, followed by updating currentBranch.
Algorithm:
  1. child = createTreeNode(node).
  2. currentNodeRef.addChild(child).
  3. Find the index of currentNodeRef in currentBranch.
  4. Remove all elements after that index.
  5. Append child to currentBranch.
Related Features: createTreeNode, TreeNode.addChild, currentBranch
Related Classes: TreeNode, ChainNode, List
Input: node: ChainNode to attach; currentBranch: mutable branch list; currentNodeRef: TreeNode intended as the parent of node.
Output: void
Pre-condition: currentNodeRef is non-null and is present in currentBranch; node is non-root.
Post-condition: child TreeNode is a child of currentNodeRef; currentBranch is the path from root through the new child.

AutoPruneStrategy::createTreeNode
Summary: Converts a ChainNode into a detached TreeNode by copying the common BaseNode fields.
Algorithm:
  1. Create a new TreeNode.
  2. Copy title, levelSeq, levelText, and content from chainnode.
  3. Set children to an empty list and parent to null.
  4. Return the new TreeNode.
Related Features: BaseNode.title, BaseNode.levelSeq, BaseNode.levelText, BaseNode.content
Related Classes: TreeNode, ChainNode
Input: chainnode: ChainNode to convert.
Output: TreeNode with the same title, level sequence, level text, and content.
Pre-condition: chainnode is non-null.
Post-condition: returned TreeNode is detached; parent is null and children is empty.

AutoPruneStrategy::addNodeAndUpdateBranch
Summary: Attaches an immediate valid ChainNode to the correct ancestor in the current branch and updates the branch so that it ends with the newly attached tree node.
Algorithm:
  1. Find the last TreeNode in currentBranch whose levelSeq equals getPrefix(node.levelSeq); this is the node's parent.
  2. If no such parent exists, throw IllegalArgumentException.
  3. Call addNodeToTree(node, currentBranch, parent).
  4. addNodeToTree truncates currentBranch after that parent and appends the new node.
Related Features: addNodeToTree, createTreeNode, inherited getPrefix/isImmNext
Related Classes: TreeNode, ChainNode, List
Input: node: ChainNode to be attached; currentBranch: mutable list of TreeNodes from root to the current node.
Output: void
Pre-condition: node is a non-root chain node; currentBranch is non-empty; the parent of node appears in currentBranch; node is an immediate valid next node.
Post-condition: node is represented by a new TreeNode, attached as a child of its parent; currentBranch now ends with that new TreeNode.

AutoPruneStrategy::isAllNotImmNodesSiblings
Summary: Determines whether all queued non-immediate nodes form an immediate sibling sequence.
Algorithm:
  1. If the queue is empty, return false (or true for a trivially empty sequence depending on caller needs).
  2. Let parentSeq = getPrefix(queue.first.levelSeq).
  3. For every subsequent node in the queue:
     a. Its getPrefix(levelSeq) must equal parentSeq.
     b. Its last level must equal the previous node's last level + 1.
  4. Return true if all satisfy these conditions; otherwise return false.
Related Features: inherited getPrefix/getLastLevel
Related Classes: Deque, ChainNode, List
Input: queue: Deque<ChainNode> containing pending nodes.
Output: true if all pending nodes are siblings with consecutive level order; false otherwise.
Pre-condition: queue is non-null.
Post-condition: no tree state is changed by this check.

AutoPruneStrategy::buildTree
Summary: Builds a TreeNode tree from a ChainNode list using the auto-prune strategy, including a pending queue for non-immediate nodes.
Algorithm:
  1. If chain is empty, create a synthetic root TreeNode with title "ROOT" and empty levelSeq, and return it.
  2. If the first chain node is root (empty levelSeq), convert it to the root and set start index to 1; otherwise create a synthetic root and start at 0.
  3. Let currentBranch = [root], pending = new ArrayDeque<ChainNode>().
  4. For each chain node cn from start index to end:
     a. If cn is an immediate valid next node for the last node in currentBranch:
           merge all pending nodes into currentBranch.last.content in arrival order;
           clear pending;
           call addNodeAndUpdateBranch(cn, currentBranch).
     b. Otherwise:
           pending.addLast(cn);
           if pending.size() == 3:
              if isAllNotImmNodesSiblings(pending) and the common parent of pending nodes is in currentBranch:
                  attach all pending nodes in order with addNodeAndUpdateBranch;
                  clear pending;
              else:
                  remove the oldest pending node and merge it into currentBranch.last.content.
  5. After processing all chain nodes, merge any remaining pending nodes into currentBranch.last.content in arrival order.
  6. Return root.
Related Features: addNodeAndUpdateBranch, isAllNotImmNodesSiblings, createTreeNode, BaseNode.concatNode, inherited isRoot/isImmNext
Related Classes: TreeNode, ChainNode, List, Deque
Input: chain: List<ChainNode> produced by ChainParser.
Output: TreeNode root of the constructed document outline.
Pre-condition: chain is non-null; if chain contains a root, it is first.
Post-condition: the returned root has title "ROOT"; regular nodes are attached according to level sequences; rejected/non-attachable nodes have been merged into content.

# Requirement
```text
## 1. Overall 

This system turns plain structured text into a document outline tree. It is intended for texts whose section headings are marked by ordered level indicators, such as Arabic numbers, Roman numerals, Chinese numerals, letters, or circled numbers. The main semantic task is to recognize heading lines, convert their numbering into comparable level sequences, preserve ordinary text as section content, and reconstruct the parent-child hierarchy of the document.

## 2. Functional Requirement

Heading recognition is pattern-driven. Patterns are tried in order, and the first valid pattern determines both the heading level sequence and its priority. A line that does not match a valid heading should be treated as content belonging to the current section. Even an empty or unmatched document should still produce a synthetic root section titled `"ROOT"`.

Number conversion should treat each supported numbering family according to its natural ordering. Roman numerals should be case-insensitive and support standard subtractive forms. Chinese numerals should support common simplified and traditional digit variants, units, large magnitudes, and signed values. Letters map alphabetically, and circled numbers map to their represented numeric value. Invalid numeric text should not create a valid heading level.

Tree construction is based on the integer level sequence of each parsed heading. A root node has an empty sequence. A child sequence extends its parent sequence, while siblings share the same prefix and advance by level order. Strict construction should reject chains that do not begin with the root. The more tolerant construction strategy should recover from irregular jumps by moving back to the nearest suitable ancestor before attaching the next node.For the auto-prune strategy, the builder should maintain the latest valid branch from the root to the current node. If the next chain node is an immediate valid next node according to the level-sequence relation, it should be attached to the nearest ancestor whose level sequence is the prefix of the new node, and the current branch should be updated.

If a chain node is not an immediate valid next node, it should be stored in a pending queue rather than attached immediately. When a later immediate node is found, pending nodes before it should be merged into the current node's content in arrival order. If the pending queue reaches three nodes, the strategy should check whether all pending nodes form an immediate sibling sequence. If so, they should be attached to the tree in order; otherwise, the oldest pending node should be merged into the current node's content. After all input nodes are processed, any remaining pending nodes should be merged into the current node's content.

When section content is merged or collected from descendants, content should be concatenated in traversal order without inserting extra separators. Parent-child links should remain consistent when tree nodes are attached.

Export behavior must be deterministic. Chain export should use one line per node in the form `LEVEL-<levelSeq>: <title>`. Tree JSON export should preserve child order and use the field names `title`, `level_seq`, `level_text`, `content`, and `children`, with stable pretty-printing using four-space indentation.

# Operation Specifications
StrictStrategy::buildTree
Summary: Builds a strict outline tree from a chain. The chain must begin with the root; otherwise construction is rejected.
Algorithm:
  1. If chain is empty, return a synthetic root TreeNode titled "ROOT".
  2. If chain is non-empty and !isRoot(chain.get(0)), throw IllegalArgumentException.
  3. root = createTreeNode(chain.get(0)); stack = [root].
  4. For each remaining ChainNode node:
     a. Search stack from the last node backward for the deepest ancestor A such that isChild(A.levelSeq, node.levelSeq).
     b. If none exists, throw IllegalArgumentException.
     c. child = createTreeNode(node); A.addChild(child).
     d. Truncate stack to the position of A, then append child.
  5. Return root.
Related Features: createTreeNode, isChild, TreeNode.addChild
Related Classes: TreeNode, ChainNode, List
Input: chain: List<ChainNode>; the first node must be the root node when non-empty.
Output: TreeNode root of the strict tree.
Pre-condition: chain is non-null.
Post-condition: The returned tree follows strict parent-child prefix relationships; invalid chains are rejected with IllegalArgumentException.

StrictStrategy::isChild
Summary: Determines whether childSeq is a direct child sequence of parentSeq.
Algorithm:
  1. If either sequence is null, return false.
  2. If childSeq.size() != parentSeq.size() + 1, return false.
  3. Return true if parentSeq equals the first parentSeq.size() elements of childSeq; otherwise false.
Related Features: none
Related Classes: List, EIntegerObject
Input: parentSeq: List<EIntegerObject>; childSeq: List<EIntegerObject>.
Output: true if childSeq extends parentSeq by exactly one level; false otherwise.
Pre-condition: both lists are non-null.
Post-condition: no state is changed.

StrictStrategy::createTreeNode
Summary: Converts a ChainNode to a detached TreeNode.
Algorithm:
  1. Create a new TreeNode.
  2. Copy title, levelSeq, levelText, and content from chainnode.
  3. Set children to an empty list and parent to null.
  4. Return the TreeNode.
Related Features: BaseNode.title, BaseNode.levelSeq, BaseNode.levelText, BaseNode.content
Related Classes: TreeNode, ChainNode
Input: chainnode: ChainNode.
Output: TreeNode with copied fields.
Pre-condition: chainnode is non-null.
Post-condition: returned TreeNode is detached.

When section content is merged or collected from descendants, content should be concatenated in traversal order without inserting extra separators. Parent-child links should remain consistent when tree nodes are attached.

Export behavior must be deterministic. Chain export should use one line per node in the form `LEVEL-<levelSeq>: <title>`. Tree JSON export should preserve child order and use the field names `title`, `level_seq`, `level_text`, `content`, and `children`, with stable pretty-printing using four-space indentation.

# Requirement
```text
## 1. Overall 

This system turns plain structured text into a document outline tree. It is intended for texts whose section headings are marked by ordered level indicators, such as Arabic numbers, Roman numerals, Chinese numerals, letters, or circled numbers. The main semantic task is to recognize heading lines, convert their numbering into comparable level sequences, preserve ordinary text as section content, and reconstruct the parent-child hierarchy of the document.

## 2. Functional Requirement

Heading recognition is pattern-driven. Patterns are tried in order, and the first valid pattern determines both the heading level sequence and its priority. A line that does not match a valid heading should be treated as content belonging to the current section. Even an empty or unmatched document should still produce a synthetic root section titled `"ROOT"`.

Number conversion should treat each supported numbering family according to its natural ordering. Roman numerals should be case-insensitive and support standard subtractive forms. Chinese numerals should support common simplified and traditional digit variants, units, large magnitudes, and signed values. Letters map alphabetically, and circled numbers map to their represented numeric value. Invalid numeric text should not create a valid heading level.

Tree construction is based on the integer level sequence of each parsed heading. A root node has an empty sequence. A child sequence extends its parent sequence, while siblings share the same prefix and advance by level order. Strict construction should reject chains that do not begin with the root. The more tolerant construction strategy should recover from irregular jumps by moving back to the nearest suitable ancestor before attaching the next node.For the auto-prune strategy, the builder should maintain the latest valid branch from the root to the current node. If the next chain node is an immediate valid next node according to the level-sequence relation, it should be attached to the nearest ancestor whose level sequence is the prefix of the new node, and the current branch should be updated.

If a chain node is not an immediate valid next node, it should be stored in a pending queue rather than attached immediately. When a later immediate node is found, pending nodes before it should be merged into the current node's content in arrival order. If the pending queue reaches three nodes, the strategy should check whether all pending nodes form an immediate sibling sequence. If so, they should be attached to the tree in order; otherwise, the oldest pending node should be merged into the current node's content. After all input nodes are processed, any remaining pending nodes should be merged into the current node's content.

When section content is merged or collected from descendants, content should be concatenated in traversal order without inserting extra separators. Parent-child links should remain consistent when tree nodes are attached.

Export behavior must be deterministic. Chain export should use one line per node in the form `LEVEL-<levelSeq>: <title>`. Tree JSON export should preserve child order and use the field names `title`, `level_seq`, `level_text`, `content`, and `children`, with stable pretty-printing using four-space indentation.

## 3. External / Tool Classes

`Utils` is an external numeric utility used by the parser for Roman numeral and Chinese numeral conversion.

# Operation Specifications
TreeExporter::exportTreeInternal
Summary: Recursively renders one TreeNode and its descendants as ASCII tree lines.
Algorithm:
  1. If isRoot is true, append node.title and a newline.
  2. Otherwise append prefix, then "-- " if isLast else "|-- ", then node.title and a newline.
  3. Compute childPrefix as prefix plus "    " if isLast else "|   ", but use "    " for root children.
  4. For each child in order, append exportTreeInternal(child, childPrefix, i == lastChild, false).
  5. Return the accumulated string.
Related Features: title, children
Related Classes: TreeNode, List
Input: node: TreeNode; prefix: String; isLast: boolean; isRoot: boolean.
Output: String containing the ASCII rendering of the subtree.
Pre-condition: node and prefix are non-null.
Post-condition: returned text preserves child order and deterministic formatting.

TreeExporter::nodeToDict
Summary: Converts a TreeNode into an ordered map suitable for JSON export.
Algorithm:
  1. Create an ordered map.
  2. Put "title" -> node.title.
  3. Put "level_seq" -> a list of integers from node.levelSeq.
  4. Put "level_text" -> node.levelText.
  5. Put "content" -> node.content.
  6. Put "children" -> a list of nodeToDict(child) for each child in node.children order.
  7. Return the map.
Related Features: title, levelSeq, levelText, content, children
Related Classes: TreeNode, List, EMap, EIntegerObject
Input: node: TreeNode.
Output: EMap with ordered keys "title", "level_seq", "level_text", "content", "children".
Pre-condition: node is non-null.
Post-condition: The map exactly represents the node and preserves child order.

TreeExporter::exportTree
Summary: Produces a deterministic ASCII-tree rendering of the document outline.
Algorithm:
  Return exportTreeInternal(tree, "", true, true).
Related Features: exportTreeInternal
Related Classes: TreeNode
Input: tree: TreeNode.
Output: String containing the ASCII tree.
Pre-condition: tree is non-null.
Post-condition: The returned string contains the root and all descendants in child order.

TreeExporter::exportToJsonFile
Summary: Writes the tree to a file in deterministic, pretty-printed JSON with four-space indentation.
Algorithm:
  1. Build an ordered map from the tree using nodeToDict.
  2. Serialize the map to a JSON string with four-space indentation and stable key ordering.
  3. Write the JSON string to filePath using UTF-8 encoding.
Related Features: nodeToDict
Related Classes: TreeNode, Path, EMap
Input: tree: TreeNode; filePath: Path.
Output: void
Pre-condition: tree is non-null; filePath is non-null and denotes a writable path.
Post-condition: The file at filePath exists and contains the JSON representation of tree.

A child sequence extends its parent sequence, while siblings share the same prefix and advance by level order. Strict construction should reject chains that do not begin with the root. The more tolerant construction strategy should recover from irregular jumps by moving back to the nearest suitable ancestor before attaching the next node.For the auto-prune strategy, the builder should maintain the latest valid branch from the root to the current node. If the next chain node is an immediate valid next node according to the level-sequence relation, it should be attached to the nearest ancestor whose level sequence is the prefix of the new node, and the current branch should be updated.

If a chain node is not an immediate valid next node, it should be stored in a pending queue rather than attached immediately. When a later immediate node is found, pending nodes before it should be merged into the current node's content in arrival order. If the pending queue reaches three nodes, the strategy should check whether all pending nodes form an immediate sibling sequence. If so, they should be attached to the tree in order; otherwise, the oldest pending node should be merged into the current node's content. After all input nodes are processed, any remaining pending nodes should be merged into the current node's content.

When section content is merged or collected from descendants, content should be concatenated in traversal order without inserting extra separators. Parent-child links should remain consistent when tree nodes are attached.

Export behavior must be deterministic. Chain export should use one line per node in the form `LEVEL-<levelSeq>: <title>`. Tree JSON export should preserve child order and use the field names `title`, `level_seq`, `level_text`, `content`, and `children`, with stable pretty-printing using four-space indentation.

## 3. External / Tool Classes

# Operation Specifications
TreeExporter::exportTreeInternal
Summary: Recursively renders one TreeNode and its descendants as ASCII tree lines.
Algorithm:
  1. If isRoot is true, append node.title and a newline.
  2. Otherwise append prefix, then "-- " if isLast else "|-- ", then node.title and a newline.
  3. Compute childPrefix as prefix plus "    " if isLast else "|   ", but use "    " for root children.
  4. For each child in order, append exportTreeInternal(child, childPrefix, i == lastChild, false).
  5. Return the accumulated string.
Related Features: title, children
Related Classes: TreeNode, List
Input: node: TreeNode; prefix: String; isLast: boolean; isRoot: boolean.
Output: String containing the ASCII rendering of the subtree.
Pre-condition: node and prefix are non-null.
Post-condition: returned text preserves child order and deterministic formatting.

TreeExporter::nodeToDict
Summary: Converts a TreeNode into an ordered map suitable for JSON export.
Algorithm:
  1. Create an ordered map.
  2. Put "title" -> node.title.
  3. Put "level_seq" -> a list of integers from node.levelSeq.
  4. Put "level_text" -> node.levelText.
  5. Put "content" -> node.content.
  6. Put "children" -> a list of nodeToDict(child) for each child in node.children order.
  7. Return the map.
Related Features: title, levelSeq, levelText, content, children
Related Classes: TreeNode, List, EMap, EIntegerObject
Input: node: TreeNode.
Output: EMap with ordered keys "title", "level_seq", "level_text", "content", "children".
Pre-condition: node is non-null.
Post-condition: The map exactly represents the node and preserves child order.

TreeExporter::exportTree
Summary: Produces a deterministic ASCII-tree rendering of the document outline.
Algorithm:
  Return exportTreeInternal(tree, "", true, true).
Related Features: exportTreeInternal
Related Classes: TreeNode
Input: tree: TreeNode.
Output: String containing the ASCII tree.
Pre-condition: tree is non-null.
Post-condition: The returned string contains the root and all descendants in child order.

TreeExporter::exportToJsonFile
Summary: Writes the tree to a file in deterministic, pretty-printed JSON with four-space indentation.
Algorithm:
  1. Build an ordered map from the tree using nodeToDict.
  2. Serialize the map to a JSON string with four-space indentation and stable key ordering.
  3. Write the JSON string to filePath using UTF-8 encoding.
Related Features: nodeToDict
Related Classes: TreeNode, Path, EMap
Input: tree: TreeNode; filePath: Path.
Output: void
Pre-condition: tree is non-null; filePath is non-null and denotes a writable path.
Post-condition: The file at filePath exists and contains the JSON representation of tree.

# Operation Specifications
ChainParser::detectLevel
Summary: Tests a line against all configured heading patterns in order; the first valid match determines the heading's level sequence and priority.
Algorithm:
  1. For each pattern p in patterns, with index i:
     a. Obtain Matcher from p.getRegex().
     b. If the matcher does not match the whole line, continue.
     c. Extract the numbering text and the visible title text from the matcher.
     d. Convert the numbering text to a level sequence using p.convertMatchedText.
     e. If conversion fails or produces an empty/invalid level sequence, continue to the next pattern.
     f. Otherwise return createChainNode(levelSeq, title, "", numberingText, i).
  2. If no pattern produces a valid heading, return null.
Related Features: patterns, createChainNode, LevelPattern.getRegex/convertMatchedText, ParserHelper
Related Classes: ChainNode, LevelPattern, Pattern, NumberType
Input: line: String containing one line of plain text.
Output: ChainNode heading descriptor with empty content, or null if the line is not a valid heading.
Pre-condition: line is non-null; patterns is ordered by priority.
Post-condition: If non-null is returned, the returned node's patternPriority is the index of the first valid matching pattern.

ChainParser::parseToChain
Summary: Parses the full text into a ChainNode list whose first element is always a synthetic root named "ROOT"; all ordinary text is retained as section content.
Algorithm:
  1. Create root = createChainNode(emptyList(), "ROOT", "", "", -1).
  2. Set current = root and content = new StringBuilder().
  3. For each line of text:
     a. heading = detectLevel(line).
     b. If heading is non-null:
           current.content = content.toString();
           chain.add(current);
           current = heading;
           content = new StringBuilder();
        else:
           append the original line to content.
  4. At the end, set current.content = content.toString(); chain.add(current).
  5. Return chain.
Related Features: detectLevel, createChainNode, BaseNode.content
Related Classes: ChainNode, List
Input: text: String containing the full plain-text document.
Output: List<ChainNode>; never empty. The first node is the synthetic root.
Pre-condition: text is non-null.
Post-condition: Every heading line is represented by a ChainNode; all non-heading lines are stored in the content of the most recent section or root.

ChainParser::createChainNode
Summary: Factory method that creates a ChainNode with the given parsed values.
Algorithm:
  1. Instantiate a new ChainNode.
  2. Set levelSeq, title, content, levelText, and patternPriority from the arguments.
  3. Return the ChainNode.
Related Features: ChainNode inherited BaseNode fields, patternPriority
Related Classes: ChainNode, List
Input: levelSeq: List<Integer>; title: String; content: String; levelText: String; patternPriority: int.
Output: A new ChainNode carrying the supplied values.
Pre-condition: levelSeq is non-null; patternPriority is -1 for synthetic root nodes and >=0 for detected headings.
Post-condition: returned ChainNode has exactly the supplied field values.

# Operation Specifications
ChainParser::detectLevel
Summary: Tests a line against all configured heading patterns in order; the first valid match determines the heading's level sequence and priority.
Algorithm:
  1. For each pattern p in patterns, with index i:
     a. Obtain Matcher from p.getRegex().
     b. If the matcher does not match the whole line, continue.
     c. Extract the numbering text and the visible title text from the matcher.
     d. Convert the numbering text to a level sequence using p.convertMatchedText.
     e. If conversion fails or produces an empty/invalid level sequence, continue to the next pattern.
     f. Otherwise return createChainNode(levelSeq, title, "", numberingText, i).
  2. If no pattern produces a valid heading, return null.
Related Features: patterns, createChainNode, LevelPattern.getRegex/convertMatchedText, ParserHelper
Related Classes: ChainNode, LevelPattern, Pattern, NumberType
Input: line: String containing one line of plain text.
Output: ChainNode heading descriptor with empty content, or null if the line is not a valid heading.
Pre-condition: line is non-null; patterns is ordered by priority.
Post-condition: If non-null is returned, the returned node's patternPriority is the index of the first valid matching pattern.

ChainParser::parseToChain
Summary: Parses the full text into a ChainNode list whose first element is always a synthetic root named "ROOT"; all ordinary text is retained as section content.
Algorithm:
  1. Create root = createChainNode(emptyList(), "ROOT", "", "", -1).
  2. Set current = root and content = new StringBuilder().
  3. For each line of text:
     a. heading = detectLevel(line).
     b. If heading is non-null:
           current.content = content.toString();
           chain.add(current);
           current = heading;
           content = new StringBuilder();
        else:
           append the original line to content.
  4. At the end, set current.content = content.toString(); chain.add(current).
  5. Return chain.
Related Features: detectLevel, createChainNode, BaseNode.content
Related Classes: ChainNode, List
Input: text: String containing the full plain-text document.
Output: List<ChainNode>; never empty. The first node is the synthetic root.
Pre-condition: text is non-null.
Post-condition: Every heading line is represented by a ChainNode; all non-heading lines are stored in the content of the most recent section or root.

ChainParser::createChainNode
Summary: Factory method that creates a ChainNode with the given parsed values.
Algorithm:
  1. Instantiate a new ChainNode.
  2. Set levelSeq, title, content, levelText, and patternPriority from the arguments.
  3. Return the ChainNode.
Related Features: ChainNode inherited BaseNode fields, patternPriority
Related Classes: ChainNode, List
Input: levelSeq: List<Integer>; title: String; content: String; levelText: String; patternPriority: int.
Output: A new ChainNode carrying the supplied values.
Pre-condition: levelSeq is non-null; patternPriority is -1 for synthetic root nodes and >=0 for detected headings.
Post-condition: returned ChainNode has exactly the supplied field values.
